newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:
* House Speaker Newt Gingrich said he would borrow from Bob Dole to pay a $300,000 fine to the House of Representatives. Under today's plan, Gingrich would not have to repay money until 2005.
* Senior administration officials said President Clinton approved a plan to reorganise the State Department, bringing three related foreign affairs agencies under its control.
* New York Governor George Pataki said Lieutenant Governor Betsy McCaughey Ross would be dropped from his Republican re-election ticket in 1998.
* British Prime Minister John Major declared his opposition to current proposals for Britain's integration into Europe, yielding to the anti-European wing of his party.
* Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to remain in power in the face of police recommendations that he be indicted for breach of public trust.
* Brooklyn Democrat Representative Charles Schumer will challenge New York Senator Alfonse D'Amato, dropping plans to run for New York state governor.
* Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic seems to be asserting his power again, taking steps to limit criticism of him in the independent news media.
* Scientific measurements indicate the universe could have an "up" and a "down", as opposed to the notion that space is uniform without north, south, up and down.
